title.narrative: Aimags and Soums Green Regional Development Investment Program - Tranche 1

description.narrative: The program represents a fundamental paradigm shift in applying a transformative model to promote green territorial development and urban-rural linkages, whereby livable human settlements - aimag (province) and soum (subunit of an aimag) centers - become anchors of green agribusinesses that promote sustainable, resilient, and high-carbon sequestration rangeland management. Initially focusing on Mongolia's western aimags, the program will promote climate finance and private sector investment mechanisms that can be replicated countrywide.

Output: Accessible financing for low-carbon and climate-resilient livestock and agro-business value chains created (financial intermediation loan component) Indicator: Under window 1, loans, subloans, or loans plus credit risk guarantees of at least $20 million provided for SME investments, of which at least 30% led by women, in targeted aimag and inter-soum centers, through PUGs and herder groups Progress/Status: As part of the project, consultations were held with the relevant ADB specialist regarding the establishment of the GIRAF Fund. Although the engagement of an individual consultant was proposed to the Project Director as a more time- and cost-efficient option, a decision was made to proceed with recruiting a consulting firm. In accordance with the Law on Investment Funds of Mongolia, the PIU is currently undertaking activities such as reviewing the legal and regulatory framework for establishing the GIRAF Fund and conducting meetings with the Financial Regulatory Commission and other relevant stakeholders. In April 2025, the Minister of Finance submitted a request to ADB to appoint “DBM Asset Management” as the Fund Manager of the GIRAF, and the bank issued an approval in May 2025. As a result, the conditions were created for finalizing the terms of reference for the tender for the Project Implementation and Management Support for Outcome 2 (PIO3). The draft terms of reference were submitted to the Development Bank for comments. The preparation of a draft quadrilateral agreement for the implementation of the project has been initiated.
As part of the project, consultations were held with the relevant ADB specialist regarding the establishment of the GIRAF Fund. Although the engagement of an individual consultant was proposed to the Project Director as a more time- and cost-efficient option, a decision was made to proceed with recruiting a consulting firm. In accordance with the Law on Investment Funds of Mongolia, we are currently undertaking activities such as reviewing the legal and regulatory framework for establishing the GIRAF Fund and conducting meetings with the Financial Regulatory Commission and other relevant stakeholders. In April 2025, the Minister of Finance submitted a request to ADB to appoint “DBM Asset Management” as the Fund Manager of the GIRAF, and the bank issued an approval in May 2025. An official letter (No.111, dated 29 August 2025) was submitted to the MED, proposing that the preparation of the documentation for the establishment of the GIRAF Fund be carried out by engaging an individual consultant. This approach was recommended as a more time- and cost-efficient alternative to contracting a consulting firm under a time-based arrangement, which would entail higher costs. The proposal further suggested that, in the event an individual consultant is engaged, the recruitment of a consulting firm could be postponed and conducted during the project implementation stage—after the Fund has been established and loan disbursement through the Fund has commenced. Following the submission of the official letter, the proposal to hire an individual consultant was presented in person several times to the Project Director at the MED and subsequently introduced to the Director of the Development Financing Department of the MOF and ADB. The Director of the Development Financing Department expressed support for the approach, noting that it would result in significant cost savings. At present, the TOR for the individual consultant have been finalized. The proposal to include this recruitment in the project's procurement plan has been submitted to the Project Director for presentation at the upcoming PSC meeting, and the PMO is currently awaiting confirmation of the meeting schedule.

Output: Climate-resilient, high-carbon sequestration, and sustainable rangeland and agricultural management implemented Indicator: Primary works for the irrigated perimeter of a 1,400-ha fodder and crop farms built, including ecosystem-based water harvesting and conservancy solutions Progress/Status: During visits to Bayan-Ulgii, Uvs, and Khovd aimags, a thorough presentation was given on the legal framework for irrigation systems, specifically addressing requirements for local ownership of headworks and main canals, land use, and water user associations. Additionally, effective strategies for operating shared technical centers, either through cooperatives or with local government support, were proposed. The team also visited several irrigation systems, including "Temee Khuzu" in Deluun soum and "Mandakhyn Am" in Buyant soum (Bayan-Ulgii Aimag), "Khar Khag" in Umnugovi soum, "Khar Tolgoi" in Tarialan soum, and "Baruunturuun" in Baruunturuun soum (Uvs Aimag), and "Khoit Gol" in Darvi soum, and "Tavan Boolt" in Erdeneburen soum (Khovd Aimag).
Under this performance indicator, implementation of 4 sub-activities is planned for the period 2025-2029. As of September 30, 2025, the progress stands at 5.09%.
